newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Angolan troops invaded its territory.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Angolan troops invaded its territory.

text.p: The Zaire government said on Friday that Angolan troops had invaded its territory close to the border with Cabinda, state radio said.

It quoted a presidential statement as saying thousands of traders and residents had fled the Zairean village of Yema, close to Muanda on the Atlantic coast and about 400 km (240 miles) west of the capital Kinshasa.
"In fact this village had been invaded since the beginning of the week by 1,400 heavily armed soldiers of the Angolan army," the radio quoted the statement as saying.
It said Angolan troops were also around Zaire's diamond trading town of Tshikapa, in Western Kasai Province. Angola

has been increasingly linked to Zaire's six-month-old conflict. Regional analysts say the Angolan government has been supporting Laurent Kabila's rebels who are trying to topple Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko who for years backed Angola's UNITA guerrillas.
